turns.speaker: Caroline
turns.text: Morning, Nate. Got a minute? I need to walk you through something I did over the weekend.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Sure, what's up? You look like you've been staring at a terminal for 48 hours.

turns.speaker: Caroline
turns.text: Basically that. I migrated the customer schema to the new normalized structure. No backup, I know, I know — I was rushing because the deadline was Monday.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Wait, no backup? That's... bold. Did it go okay?

turns.speaker: Caroline
turns.text: Define 'okay.' The migration corrupted a bunch of customer records — addresses got shuffled between accounts, some phone numbers ended up in the email field. It's a mess.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Oh no. Can you restore from the nightly backup?

turns.speaker: Caroline
turns.text: That's the worst part. The corruption spread to the backups — the script that runs the backup was pulling from the same live tables during the migration window. It took me two days to repair the backup chain. We're only now back to a clean state.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Two days? That's brutal. So what's the plan going forward?

turns.speaker: Caroline
turns.text: I've already set up point-in-time recovery snapshots independent of the main backup system. So even if the main backup gets corrupted again, we can roll back to any minute. That's my safety net now.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Good. And please tell me you're not going to deploy anything else without running the test suite first.

turns.speaker: Caroline
turns.text: Yeah... about that. I deployed the new schema change without running the test suite. That's how the regression slipped into production — the one that broke the customer search. I'm not proud of it.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Caroline. We have a test suite for a reason. But okay, what's done is done. How do we prevent this from happening again?

turns.speaker: Caroline
turns.text: I've already set up a CI gate that blocks merges without tests. From now on, untested code never reaches production. That's non-negotiable.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Alright. Let's hope that's enough. But seriously, next time — backup first, tests second.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Hey, Caroline. How's the customer data looking after last week's fiasco?

turns.speaker: Caroline
turns.text: Actually, much better. I took a full snapshot before the migration this time — that was the lesson I learned. So even if something goes wrong, the migration can always be rolled back to that snapshot.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Nice. So you're covered on the rollback front.

turns.speaker: Caroline
turns.text: Exactly. And the CI gate is working — I've already seen two PRs get blocked because they didn't include tests. The team is grumbling, but it's working.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Good. Grumbling is better than a production outage. So you're feeling confident about the next migration?

turns.speaker: Caroline
turns.text: I am. Snapshot before, tests enforced, point-in-time recovery in place. I think we're solid.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Famous last words. But I'll take it.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Morning. You look like you've been up all night again. What happened?

turns.speaker: Caroline
turns.text: The snapshot approach — it turns out that wasn't enough. We had a minor schema tweak yesterday, and the snapshot I took before the migration was already stale by deploy time. The data had changed in the two hours between snapshot and rollout, so rolling back would have lost those updates.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Oh, that's a classic. So what did you do?

turns.speaker: Caroline
turns.text: I was wrong about the snapshot being sufficient. We replaced it with continuous replication — we're now streaming every change to a separate replica in real time. So if we need to roll back, we can go to any point, not just the snapshot moment.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: That's a much better safety net. So the snapshot is gone?

turns.speaker: Caroline
turns.text: We keep it as a baseline, but the continuous replication is the real protection now. Snapshots go stale by deploy time — that's the lesson. Continuous replication doesn't.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Good call. And the CI gate is still holding?

turns.speaker: Caroline
turns.text: Yep, untested code never reaches production. That part's solid. It's just the data safety that needed the upgrade.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Well, I'm glad you figured it out before the next big migration. Let's grab coffee — you look like you need it.

turns.speaker: Caroline
turns.text: Deal.
